thesis.problem: Most factory work that is still done by hand is high-mix, unstructured and safety-critical, which is exactly the work conventional industrial automation has never been able to take on. A traditional robot cell is programmed for one task on one line, costs six figures before it moves, and stops earning the day the product changes, so the mid-sized manufacturers who make up most of German industry have largely stayed out.
thesis.solution: RobCo builds modular robots and the software that makes them autonomous, combining perception, motion planning and self-learning so a system can handle machine tending, palletising, dispensing and welding without being reprogrammed for every variant. It is sold as robotics-as-a-service with no upfront investment, which moves the cost from capital expenditure to a monthly line, and its Alfie robot is built for the whole autonomous industrial lifecycle rather than a single station.

sources.title: Munich-based RobCo becomes a robotics unicorn as valuation doubles in nine months
sources.quote: RobCo, a Munich-based robotics startup focused on industrial automation, today announced that it has surpassed an €892.4 million ($1 billion) valuation in a transaction that combines new investment and an employee secondary share sale.

sources.title: Munich-based RobCo becomes a robotics unicorn as valuation doubles in nine months
sources.quote: Earlier this year, in January, the company raised €89.2 million ($100 million) in a Series C round co-led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Lingotto Innovation.
